aura: Awe through the single-eyed heavenly kami identity (c07/c10), force of the documented ironworking (c06) and very close low camera; sparks are physical forge effects.
artistic_choices: Select the documented identification with one-eyed Amenomahitotsu from c07/c10, not etymology alone. Single central eye placement interprets the one-eyed variant; placement is not asserted as a source fact.
Fully opaque charcoal work robes, leather apron, aged face, hammer and tongs are editorial smithing-scene presentation, not specific sourced iconography.
No giant body size asserted; tightly cropped low-angle torso makes him imposing. Cloud horizon and palette are atmospheric editorial choices for the heavenly setting.
No documented fire control: hot metal and sparks depict normal ironworking, not an added magical power. Respectful awe for living Shinto tradition.
Targeted edit removes accidental lateral eyes/sockets so the selected documented one-eyed variant has exactly one eye.
prompt: Edit ONLY the face anatomy of Amatsumara in this illustration. The kami must have EXACTLY ONE EYE TOTAL: preserve the existing single central eye on the forehead. Completely REMOVE BOTH lateral eyes AND BOTH lateral eye sockets AND BOTH lateral eyebrows from the normal human eye positions; replace them with continuous smooth weathered forehead/upper-cheek skin, with no slits, hollows, scars or lids. There must be only the central eye above his nose; no second or third eye anywhere. Keep all other features and the whole composition exactly unchanged: opaque robes, leather apron, two arms and hands, hammer striking hot iron on rock, forging sparks, divine rocky heavenly setting, painterly cinematic lighting. No text, signatures, watermarks, borders, extra limbs or generic magic aura.
rationale: Every illustration must feel 'sangar': dangerous, imposing or awe-inspiring, with the being as the undeniable subject. The owner rejected earlier images that read as an ordinary person, an ordinary animal, an empty landscape, or a calm, cute or decorative portrait. Those outcomes are failures regardless of technical quality.
